lines.para: **Sunday 4 March, 1.40 p.m.:** Sergei Skripal and his daughter Yulia, who arrived from Moscow the day before, park their car in the town centre. They go to the pub, then have lunch at a restaurant until 3.35 p.m.
**4.15 p.m.:** a passer-by calls for help. Father and daughter have been found unconscious on a bench. An army nurse who happened to be passing gives them first aid.
**5.10 p.m.:** Yulia is flown out by helicopter, her father taken by road. A police officer who came to the scene falls ill in turn.
**12 March:** Prime Minister Theresa May announces that a military-grade nerve agent of the “Novichok” type, developed in Russia, was used. She judges Moscow’s responsibility “highly likely”.
**14 March:** London expels twenty-three Russian diplomats. Moscow denies any involvement.
**26 March:** more than a hundred Russian diplomats are expelled by some twenty allied countries. France sends four home. Father and daughter are still in a critical condition.

lines.text: September 2018: two suspects identified. Sergei and Yulia Skripal survived.
